note: S120i — the dop- cluster, first of the K-8 Tier C/D backlog. Three of the six convert against engines already in the course; dop-01-02 (grouping symbols), dop-03-03 (interpreting remainders) and dop-05-03 (dividing decimals) are declined, with reasons recorded in KNOWN_ISSUES. Every conceptTag here is a load-bearing remediation target whose best experience was Tier C or D.

conversions.capability: columnCalc multiply (multidigit-multiply — was Tier D) — authored predict preserved, it already hands off to 23 × 5

widget.prompt: The first row of 23 × 45 is 23 × 5. Work it column by column, right to left, and carry when a column passes 9.

commonResults.feedback: 15 is 3 × 5 with the carry left stranded and the tens column never done. The 15 means one TEN and five ones: the 5 stays in the ones column and the 1 has to travel left to join 2 × 5.
105 has both columns multiplied but the carry never added in. 2 × 5 = 10, and the 1 carried from the ones column makes it 11 — so the row is 115, not 105.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Start at the ones: 3 × 5 = 15, so 5 stays and 1 carries. Then 2 × 5 = 10, plus the carried 1.
widget.successFeedback: 115. That is one row of the two — and the carry is why it is not simply 10 and 15 written side by side. The second row will be 23 × 40, not 23 × 4, which is where the placeholder zero comes from.

conversions.capability: columnCalc decimal add (align-points — was Tier C)

widget.prompt: Add 3.50 + 1.75. The columns are already lined up by place — work right to left and carry whenever a column passes 9.

commonResults.feedback: 4.25 has the hundredths right but the carry never left the tenths. 5 tenths + 7 tenths is 12 tenths, which is one WHOLE and 2 tenths — the whole belongs in the ones column.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Start at the hundredths, the rightmost column, and work left. Carry whenever a column total passes 9.
widget.successFeedback: 5.25. Notice that 3.5 had to be read as 3.50 for the columns to line up — and that once they do, nothing about this is different from adding whole numbers. "Line up the points" is only ever "line up the places".

predict.prompt: To add 3.5 + 1.75 in columns, the 3.5 first has to be written as…

options.label: 3.5, with the digits pushed to the right to fill the gap

predict.reveal: 3.50 — because 3.5 has no hundredths, and a column with nothing in it is a column holding zero. Pushing the digits right instead would put the 5 under the 5 of 1.75, adding tenths to hundredths. The point is what marks the places; padding just says the empty ones out loud.

conversions.capability: columnCalc decimal add (decimal-regroup — was Tier C)

widget.prompt: Add 0.75 + 3.80, column by column. Start at the hundredths and carry when a column passes 9.

commonResults.feedback: 3.55 leaves the carry behind. 7 tenths + 8 tenths is 15 tenths — one whole and 5 tenths — so the 5 stays in the tenths but the whole has to move into the ones column, making 4 wholes, not 3.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Hundredths first: 5 + 0. Then the tenths, 7 + 8, which passes 9 and carries. Then the ones.
widget.successFeedback: 4.55. The carry crossed the decimal point, from tenths into ones, and behaved exactly as a carry from tens into hundreds would. The point does not interrupt the columns — it only names where they stop being whole.

predict.prompt: Adding 0.75 + 3.80, the tenths column gives 7 + 8 = 15 tenths. That carry will travel…

options.label: Across the decimal point, into the ones column
Nowhere — a carry cannot cross the decimal point

predict.reveal: Straight across into the ones. Fifteen tenths is one whole and five tenths, and "one whole" belongs on the other side of the point. The decimal point is a label on the places, not a wall between them — carries cross it exactly as they cross from tens into hundreds.
